Aśmagīta : nt.: Name of an ancient Itihāsa 12. 28. 2.

In this Itihāsa, the Brāhmaṇa Aśman, when questioned by king Janaka of Videha who was overcome by grief how one shold face the acquistition and loss of relatives and wealth, instructed him 12. 2

Aśmaka : m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people.

A. Location: Listed by Saṁjaya among the (southern) Janapadas of Bhāratavarṣa (ata ūrdhvaṁ janapadān nibodha gadato mama) 6. 10. 37, 5; (aśmakāḥ pāṁsurāṣṭrāś ca) 6. 10. 42.

B. Epic events:

(1) Listed by Dhṛtarāṣṭra among those who were defeated by Karṇa before the Vaiṣṇava sacrifice of Duryodhana and were made to pay tribute (aśmakān ṛṣikāṁs tathā/yo jitvā samare vīraś cakre balibhṛtaḥ purā//) 8. 5. 20 (a reference to what is hinted in 3. 241. 16, but Aśmakas are not specifically mentioned in the report of Karṇa's conquest as detailed in Vol. IV, App.

-72, pp. 1078-1079);

(2) Listed by Dhṛtarāṣṭra among those who fought on the side of the Pāṇḍavas (aśmakāḥ kekayāś caiva) 7. 61. 39; (the king of the Aśmakas referred to as aśmakeśvara 7. 36. 23 and as aśmakadāyāda 7. 36. 21).
